title: Gideon and the Spire
premise: Theo Iversen, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics they carve, has survived the Thornfell mountains by staying invisible—until prayers whispered at old shrines start being answered, and the dead begin screaming about a thing wearing King Aldric's crown. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors and courted by a resurgent cult of the old gods, Theo joins forces with Serah Vane, a disgraced royal justiciar who believes justice should outlive the law that exiled her. Together they trace the corruption to the Spire, an ancient god-prison beneath the capital where a bound deity has been slowly devouring the king's soul to buy its freedom. In the end, Theo must choose between using their gift to unbind the god entirely—which would grant it the power to remake the world—or shattering the Spire forever, killing the old gods' last voice and severing Theo from the dead they love; they choose the shattering, and Serah chooses them over her restored title.
about_author: Kestrel Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archaeologist who spent six years cataloguing burial goods in mountain monasteries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about the voices history leaves behind, and claim every novel begins with an object that refuses to stay silent.

chapters.title: The Bone That Sang
chapters.summary: Theo Iversen carves a funeral relic for a dying smuggler and hears, for the first time in years, not the man's memories but a stranger's scream: 'the crown is hollow.' POV: Theo. Emotional beat: unease—the safe invisibility of Theo's life cracks open.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: In the village of Lowmark, a shrine long silent grants a child's prayer—and takes the mother's memory as payment. Theo investigates the trade routes and finds every old shrine along the Thornfell roads humming again. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: dread deepening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Justiciar's Fall
chapters.summary: Serah Vane is stripped of her office for refusing to burn a shrine-keeper who turned out to be innocent. She rides into the mountains hunting answers the capital forbids. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: bitter resolve; justice without a badge.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Serah ambushes Theo on a hidden pass, mistaking them for a cult courier. A standoff becomes an uneasy alliance when the dead in Theo's pack corroborate her evidence against the Crown. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grudging respect between opposites.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Theo reads a century-old bone relic and uncovers the truth: the Spire beneath the capital was built to imprison a god, and every king since has fed it soul-memories to keep it sleeping. Aldric has stopped feeding it—it feeds itself now. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Cole
chapters.summary: Crown inquisitor Cole burns the Lowmark shrine and posts warrants for 'the bone-witch.' Theo's network of smugglers scatters; one dies buying Theo time to escape. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: guilt—invisibility has a body count.

chapters.title: The Cult of the Open Door
chapters.summary: A cult of the old gods offers Theo sanctuary, claiming the unbinding of the Spire will free humanity from divine abandonment. Their leader, Mother Cassia, knows too much about Theo's gift. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: temptation—a home that wants something back.

chapters.title: Duty's Weight
chapters.summary: Serah receives a pardon offer: return, denounce Theo, and be reinstated. She burns the letter but can't stop rehearsing what she'd say. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: love against duty, first acknowledged even to herself.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: At a border garrison, Theo glimpses King Aldric on progress and hears nothing from him—not silence, but absence, like a house after the family has left. The thing wearing the crown looks directly at Theo across the courtyard. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Bargains in Bone
chapters.summary: To learn the Spire's wards, Theo must read a relic carved by the prison's original architect—but the price is carrying the architect's dying madness for a night. Serah keeps watch, talking Theo back to themselves at dawn. POV: both. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in damage.

chapters.title: Mother Cassia's Truth
chapters.summary: Cassia reveals the cult doesn't want the god freed—they want to merge with it, and they need a hearer like Theo as the key. Theo flees the sanctuary, stealing the architect's map. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: betrayal; no refuge is neutral.

chapters.title: The Road to the Capital
chapters.summary: Theo and Serah descend out of the Thornfell together, pursued by both Cole's inquisitors and Cassia's faithful. A running battle through the river gorges costs them their supplies and nearly each other. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: trust tested under fire and holding.

chapters.title: City of Quiet Bells
chapters.summary: The capital feels wrong: bells ring but no one remembers why, and beggars pray to shrines that answer too readily. Serah uses her old contacts; Theo listens to the city's dead, who all repeat one phrase: 'the door is almost open.' POV: both. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Queen Isolde privately reveals she has known for a year that her husband is gone; she has kept the kingdom running while the thing in his shape signs decrees. She gives them the Spire's entrance key—for a promise that Aldric's soul gets rest either way. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: compassion complicating the mission.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Through the undercrofts and drowned stairways, the pair enters the Spire. The dead here are not echoes but prisoners, and they cling to Theo begging to be carried out. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the weight of hearing—gift become burden.

chapters.title: Cole's Judgment
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Cole corners them at the Spire gate, but the god's leaking presence shows him visions of every execution he's performed; shattered, he lets them pass—or falls to his own doubt. POV: Cole. Emotional beat: the corrupter corrupted; power devouring its servant.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Deep in the Spire, Aldric's remnant soul still fights. He begs Theo to end it before the god wears him fully into the world above. The god speaks through his mouth, offering Theo everything the dead could give. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the seduction of power made personal.

chapters.title: Cassia Ascendant
chapters.summary: The cult breaches the Spire behind them; Cassia begins the merging rite, forcing the crisis early. Serah holds the stair alone against the faithful while Theo reaches the binding-stone. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: duty redefined—she protects a person, not a law.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: At the heart of the Spire, Theo faces the choice: unbind the god and gain the power to remake everything—including bringing back the dead they love—or shatter the binding forever. They remember every voice they've ever carried, and swing the hammer. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: sacrifice; love means letting go.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: The Spire collapses inward; the god unravels, Cassia's rite fails mid-word, and Aldric dies human at last. Theo wakes deaf to the dead for the first time since childhood—and grieves the quiet like a wound. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: hollow victory, grief and relief entangled.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: With the king dead and the succession uncertain, Serah refuses restoration to a Crown that burned innocents; instead she stands witness at public hearings for the shrine-keepers, building accountability the law never allowed. The new regency, uneasy, permits it. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: justice rebuilt from ruins.

chapters.title: The Carver's Hands
chapters.summary: Months later, Theo carves a simple memorial stone in Lowmark—hears nothing, and smiles anyway. Serah arrives on the mountain road with no warrant and no title, only a question about where the road goes next. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: quiet hope; two people choosing each other beyond duty.
